Job Description

As our Pensions Writer, you'll combine genuine pensions expertise with strong editorial judgement to turn complex rules, choices and industry changes into clear, useful content for our customers. You'll have pensions and retirement planning at the heart of your work, while also covering the investment, personal finance and economic issues that shape people's financial futures. Across articles, guides, newsletters, podcasts and video, you'll help people understand their options, make informed decisions and build the confidence that's at the heart of Feel Good Investing.

What you'll do

  • Research, write and edit engaging pensions and retirement content for our website, app, newsletters, guides and other customer communications.
  • Turn complex subjects such as pension tax rules, retirement income, drawdown, annuities, the State Pension, auto-enrolment, contribution allowances and pension transfers into clear, accessible content.
  • Stay on top of pensions legislation, regulation, government policy and industry developments, identifying the changes and topics that matter to customers.
  • Write across related personal finance and investment subjects, including ISAs, tax, savings, markets, inflation and interest rates.
  • Bring your pensions expertise to different formats, developing ideas and content for articles, campaigns, podcasts, videos and webinars.
  • Work closely with editorial, marketing, PR, product, technical and compliance colleagues to make sure our content is accurate, balanced and engaging.
  • Use audience insight, search trends and performance data to understand what works and continually improve our content.

What you'll bring

  • Proven experience writing about pensions, retirement planning or long-term savings, with the pensions knowledge to write confidently and authoritatively for a broad audience.
  • Strong knowledge of the UK pensions landscape, including defined contribution pensions, SIPPs, workplace pensions, pension tax rules and retirement options.
  • The ability to make complex or technical subjects clear, accurate and engaging, supported by excellent writing, editing and proofreading skills.
  • Sound editorial judgement and an understanding of how accessible financial content needs to work within regulatory and compliance requirements.
  • An interest in personal finance, investing and the wider economy, and the confidence to work with subject matter experts to question and clarify technical detail where needed.
  • Your pensions writing experience could have been gained in journalism, financial services, a pension provider or investment platform, consultancy, an agency or another content-focused environment. What's important is your ability to write clearly and authoritatively about pensions for a broad audience.
  • Experience writing for retail investors or consumer finance audiences would be useful, as would knowledge of financial promotions and Consumer Duty.
  • Familiarity with SEO, digital publishing or content performance tools, or experience creating newsletters, guides, scripts, podcasts or video content, would be an advantage.

About us

We are a leading integrated media and marketing services company at the heart of a community of over 590,000 UK healthcare professionals. With more than 30 years of experience, we produce industry-leading content and experiences through our award-winning brands, publications, and events. We produce trusted, data-driven content that informs and inspires healthcare professionals across the UK and Europe. We are a Great Place to Work and UK's Best Workplaces for Women certified employer, offering a range of benefits including 28 days annual leave (rising to 30 days after 2 years) excluding bank holidays, private healthcare insurance, flexible working and more.

The Role

Our Community Data Administrator will be responsible for the quality, coverage, depth and development of the organisation's HCP community. The role will ensure we have a high-quality, accurate, comprehensive, current, relevant and growing audience that meets the needs of the business and our clients.

They will develop a detailed understanding of the organisation's HCP data and the wider addressable HCP market, identifying where we have strong coverage, where gaps exist and what actions we can take to address them. They will use first- and third-party data, market intelligence and behavioural and engagement data to understand the composition and health of our community and identify opportunities for growth and improvement.

This is a highly analytical role for someone who loves working with data, numbers and solving problems. They will interrogate datasets, spot patterns and anomalies, assess data quality and freshness, identify gaps and translate findings into clear actions.

Working closely with teams across the organisation, they will help source and evaluate new data, improve HCP profiling and segmentation, strengthen our understanding of audience engagement and ensure our HCP community becomes increasingly accurate, complete, current and commercially valuable.

Location: Central London (Hybrid)

Reporting to: Digital Director

Expected start date: January 2027

Salary: £30,000 to £38,000 per annum, depending on experience

Key Responsibilities:

Data Quality & Governance

Take ownership of the overall health of the organisation's HCP database, including accuracy, completeness, recency, duplication, consistency, consent and compliance. Establish clear definitions and standards for data quality and regularly measure the database against them, including agreed definitions for active HCPs, inactive HCPs, dormant records, complete profiles and verified HCPs. Identify data quality issues and work with relevant teams to implement solutions and continually improve the reliability of our data.

HCP Coverage & Gap Analysis

Build a detailed understanding of the organisation's coverage of the HCP market and identify gaps by profession, specialty, geography, seniority and other relevant characteristics. Develop clear, data-led plans to address priority audience gaps and measure the impact of actions taken.

Data Enrichment

Identify opportunities to enhance existing HCP records with additional data points and attributes, improving the completeness and depth of our profiles. Determine which additional attributes would provide the greatest audience, editorial and commercial value and identify appropriate sources for obtaining them.

Data Freshness & Engagement

Assess how recently and frequently HCPs interact with the organisation across our brands, websites, newsletters, events, CPD platforms, surveys and other products. Develop and maintain an HCP engagement scoring methodology that combines behavioural signals across the business to provide a consistent view of audience engagement. Use engagement and recency data to understand the active audience within our overall community and identify opportunities to increase engagement.

Audience Re-engagement & Cleansing

Identify inactive, ageing, duplicate, incomplete or low-confidence records. Work with relevant teams to determine appropriate approaches for re-engagement, verification, consolidation, suppression or removal. Monitor the effectiveness of re-engagement and cleansing activity and use the findings to continually improve our approach.

Data Matching & Deduplication

Develop approaches for identifying duplicate HCP records and matching individuals across different the organisation datasets, platforms and data sources. Investigate conflicting information and establish appropriate rules for determining the most reliable and current information. Support the development of an increasingly consistent and accurate single view of each HCP across the organisation.

Segmentation & Audience Insight

Develop meaningful HCP segments based on profession, specialty, geography, seniority, demographics, behaviour, engagement, recency and other relevant characteristics. Analyse these segments to identify patterns, opportunities and changes in audience behaviour. Translate complex data into clear insights that can be understood and acted upon by teams across the business.

Data Acquisition & Gap Closure

Research and evaluate new first- and third-party data sources that could strengthen the organisation's HCP community. Hours: Full Time. 35-hour working week

About Us:

The Royal Geographical Society (with the Institute of British Geographers) is the learned society and professional body for geography and geographers. It is also a charity and a membership organisation. The Society was founded in 1830 and has been one of the most active of the learned societies ever since. It was pivotal in establishing geography as a teaching and research discipline in British universities and continues to play a key role in geographical and environmental education.

About You and the Role

The RGS-IBG publish five peer-reviewed geography journals, four of which are managed by the RGS-IBG Managing Editor: Transactions of the Institute of British Geographers (TIBG), The Geographical Journal, Area, and Geo: Geography and Environment. The Society also publishes an open-access Book Series with LSE Press, the blog Geography Directions and a series of guides and advice on publishing.

The editorial assistant will report to the Managing Editor of Academic Publications, providing support for this suite of publications.

This is an exciting opportunity to develop a greater understanding of the academic peer review and publishing process and provides an excellent opportunity to work with the academic community.

The role is ideally suited to someone with very strong organisational and communication skills and an understanding and interest in contemporary academic geography.

Duties and responsibilities

Administrative tasks:

  • Lead on screening for all journal submissions – conducting initial checks for anonymity,word length, formatting, (mis)use of AI, publishing integrity issues.
  • Maintain a record of all submitted papers.
  • Lead on checking files of accepted papers for production.
  • Assist authors with generating alt text for images and figures.
  • Support Managing Editor with day-to-day author and peer reviewer communication and inbox management.
  • Assist Managing Editor with proofreading accepted papers.
  • Support Managing Editor with finding potential peer reviewers for submitted papers.
  • Oversee Special Section administration and regularly liaise with Special Section organisers.
  • Upload blog posts to the Geography Directions WordPress website.
  • Responsibility for registering DOI numbers for blog posts and online resources.
  • Design and format guides and resources for the RGS website.
  • Support with social media strategy for the journals and the Book Series.
  • Schedule editorial board meetings and take minutes.
  • Assist with annual journal prize administration.
  • Organise book launch events for Book Series authors.
  • Support the journals’ and Book Series’ events at the RGS Annual Conference.
  • Support Managing Editor to run workshops for postgraduate students and early-career researchers.

Writing and editing tasks:

  • Work with selected authors to write monthly research spotlights on journal articles for the
  • RGS website.
  • Assess and edit blog submissions to Geography Directions blog from academic authors.

Selection Criteria

Essential

  • An undergraduate degree or equivalent in Geography
  • Demonstrable knowledge of contemporary academic geography
  • An interest in scholarly publishing
  • Excellent attention to detail
  • Systematic approach to tasks
  • Strong written language skills
  • Strong organisational skills
  • Ability to prioritise and balance multiple everyday tasks at once
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team
  • Basic familiarity with Excel
  • Capability of working across multiple online platforms

Desirable

  • Experience of writing for public audiences
  • Proofreading experience
  • Administrative experience
  • Proven record of working effectively to deadlines
  • Ability to take initiative
  • Awareness of the (mis)use of AI in scholarly publishing

Salary and Benefits:

This is a permanent, full-time post subject to successful completion of a probationary period of three months. The salary range for this post is £31,200- £32,930 per annum depending on experience and qualifications. The post is based in Kensington, London.

Job Introduction

At Turning Point, we support people across The UK with Mental Health, Substance Use and Learning Disabilities. As a Youth Support Worker, you will ensure that young people living in Turning Point’s supported accommodation are supported to thrive and reach their full potential in a safe, nurturing, and supportive environment, increasing their independency to create a positive move on into the community.

As a Youth Support Worker, you will join The Lancashire Young People supported accommodation services that supports 18 young people across two locations in Chorley (Parker House and The Bridge).

Role Responsibility

You will be supporting Young People to manage their finances, gain independent living skills, promote health, wellbeing and healthy lifestyle choices as well as supporting them to maximise their involvement in local training, education, and employment opportunities.  

The role is changeable, and every day will be different, some examples of what you will be responsible for are:

  • Managing the referrals, sign up,  support and move on for the Young People
  • Developing, implementing and reviewing individual support plans and risk assessments focussing on young people’s needs, strengths and goals.
  • Providing support with budgets and finances
  • Completing accurate and detailed daily records for the Young People
  • Providing practical support and guidance to the Young People including daily living skills, cooking, cleaning, and ‘moving on’ plans
  • Supporting the Young People and landlords with housing management tasks addressing practical aspects of living in supported housing, including managing repairs, tenancies, income and anti-social behaviour.
  • Prioritising your own case load and using your initiative to plan and implement agreed actions
  • Building and maintaining relationships with a range of other professionals to work together to aim for positive outcomes for the Young People
  • Turning Point responds to the needs of the individuals and some of the tasks are therefore unpredictable. It is expected that the Youth Support Worker will work in a flexible way when required and undertake tasks that are not specifically covered within the job description, which can include cover for colleagues as required.

The Ideal Candidate

As a Youth Support Worker, we are looking for candidates who have knowledge and experience of working with young people with complex needs, homelessness, children who are looked after and in transition to leaving care or care leavers.

We’re ideally looking for a person with a NVQ level 3 or equivalent in Social Care, Youth Support Work or Housing/Homelessness, however this is not essential for the role. We are also looking for people with a background of working with young people and an understanding of homelessness and the impact this has on the wellbeing of Young People.

Ideally you will have experience in support planning, re-engaging and motivating young people to participate in employment and work programmes, education, training, volunteering, and skill building opportunities.

You need to be a great team player with lots of energy, you’ll need strong communication skills, a flexible approach and positive attitude to achieve targets in a challenging environment which requires empathy, understanding and patience.

Shift patterns

The service is staffed 24 hours a day / 7 days a week. As a Youth Support worker, you must be flexible to the service needs which include days/evenings and weekend working.

About us

As a leading health and social care provider with more than 300 locations across England, we take real pride in the services we offer.

We run all of our services on a not-for-profit basis; instead, we invest every penny back into our services and people. We never stop believing in change for the better, and we work constantly to improve the lives of the people we support.

What Benefits Will I Receive?

We know reward looks different to each person and so whether its ways to make your money go further, a culture supporting recognition and celebration, or opportunities to boost your career – we want to support you in every way we can with our total reward package.

You will get 31 days’ paid holiday a year, increasing with each year of service up to 33 days. Plus the option to buy additional holidays and spread the cost.

Location: Remote Role (The Candidate can live anywhere in England) but must be prepared to travel nationally with access to a full licence and vehicle.

Salary: £35,000 per annum plus £3,715 car allowance

Vacancy Type: Permanent, Full Time (37.5 hours per week)

We’re looking for a Communications & Events Partner to take the lead on planning and delivering some of Stonewater’s key corporate events and colleague engagement activities.

From our annual Company Day and One Connect sessions to leadership activities and wider corporate events, you’ll create engaging experiences that bring colleagues together, strengthen connections and help bring our organisational priorities to life.

This is a varied, hands-on role where you’ll take an event from the initial idea right through to delivery and evaluation. One day you could be shaping an agenda and working with senior leaders on content, and the next you might be coordinating suppliers, managing event technology or making sure everything is ready for the big day.

What you’ll be doing

You’ll:

  • Lead the planning and delivery of corporate events, taking ownership from concept through to evaluation.
  • Develop creative event ideas, formats and experiences that engage colleagues and support our priorities.
  • Coordinate venues, suppliers, logistics, audiovisual production, digital platforms and event materials.
  • Create engaging communications, presentations, agendas, scripts and speaker briefings.
  • Work closely with senior leaders, including our Chief Executive and Chief Officer Group, helping shape content and event experiences.
  • Manage event plans, schedules, expenditure and delivery timelines.
  • Use digital and audience engagement tools to make our events accessible, professional and engaging.
  • Gather feedback and evaluate our events to continually improve the experience and demonstrate value.

What we’re looking for

You’ll have experience of event management, with the confidence to manage events of varying sizes and complexity and keep multiple priorities moving at once. You’ll be a strong project manager and excellent organiser, but just as importantly, you’ll be creative, proactive and comfortable building relationships with people at all levels.

You’ll also bring:

  • Experience of planning and delivering events.
  • Excellent project management and organisational skills.
  • Strong written communication skills, with experience drafting and editing content.
  • The confidence to work with and influence senior stakeholders.
  • A good understanding of communications channels and digital tools.
  • Experience working with external suppliers, venues or production partners.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to remain calm and solutions-focused when plans change.
  • Confidence using Microsoft 365, particularly PowerPoint and Teams.

You’ll need to be comfortable working independently and taking ownership, while knowing when to involve others.

Please note: Travel is an important part of the role, with events taking place across Stonewater’s national geography. There will be travel and attendance at key events, venue visits and site inspections. You’ll therefore need a UK driving licence with business insurance and be happy to travel regularly as part of the role.

If you’re an organised, creative events professional who enjoys bringing people together and wants the opportunity to shape engaging experiences across a national organisation, we’d love to hear from you.

Stonewater is one of the UK’s largest social housing providers, driven by our purpose that everyone has a place to call home. Be a hero to a young person in care!

Are you looking for a meaningful, long-term volunteering role where you can make a positive difference in a young person’s life?

If yes, we have the perfect opportunity for you!

We’re seeking compassionate, reliable adults to become Independent Visitors - volunteer mentors and trusted friends to children and young people in care.

What is an Independent Visitor?

An Independent Visitor (IV) is a volunteer befriender and mentor who visits a young person in care once a month, usually on weekends, to enjoy fun, supportive activities together. As an IV, you’ll be a consistent, caring adult outside their professional network - someone who chooses to be there, just for them.

This is a long-term role, and we ask volunteers to commit to at least two years to help build a strong, stable relationship.

We’re especially keen to hear from volunteers based in or near London, Croydon and Kent, where many of our young people live.

Why it matters

Young people in care often face instability and frequent change. Having a consistent adult who listens, encourages and simply spends time with them can be life changing.

“My IV is the one person who’s always there for me. They make me feel like I matter.” Young Person in Care.

Who can volunteer?

You don’t need previous experience - just the right values and commitment. We’re looking for caring people who are:

  • Friendly and approachable
  • Patient, empathetic and consistent
  • A good listener
  • Committed to visiting once a month for at least two years
  • Willing to complete training and safeguarding checks

We particularly welcome applications from male volunteers and individuals from Black, Asian and other underrepresented communities.

What will you be doing?

As an Independent Visitor, you’ll:

  • Meet your young person once a month for activities like going to the cinema, bowling, exploring parks or just having a chat
  • Suggest age-appropriate outings based on their interests
  • Keep in touch between visits with a weekly call or message (if they’d like)
  • Occasionally join in on group events
  • Create meaningful, lasting memories

Please note that all travel and activity expenses will be covered.

Training & ongoing support

Before you start, we’ll provide:

  • Full initial training
  • Ongoing support and one-to-one supervision
  • Access to additional training through Southwark’s volunteer resources

Contact information

  • For an informal discussion about the role, please contact Sav D’Souza via email at .uk

Recruitment timeline

  • Applications reviewed on an ongoing basis.
  • Interviews: To be confirmed.

The closing date is given as a guide. We reserve the right to close this vacancy once a sufficient number of applications has been received. We strongly advise you to complete your application as soon as possible to avoid disappointment.

Ready to make a difference?

If you’re looking for a rewarding, long-term volunteering opportunity where you can support a young person one to one and help them thrive, we’d love to receive an application from you today!

Additional Information

Location: Aldgate, London

About Us:

ITN Solicitors is a leading Criminal, Civil Liberties and Human Rights firm with a long-standing commitment to legal aid. We have acted in some of the most high-profile cases in recent years. Most of our work is publicly funded, although our private client base has also grown in recent years.

Job Summary

We are looking for a Receptionist to manage our front desk on a daily basis and to perform a variety of administrative tasks. You will work closely with our current receptionist and be the first point of contact for our firm.

Our Receptionist’s duties include offering administrative support across the Practice. You will welcome guests and greet people who visit the business. You will also coordinate front-desk activities, including distributing correspondence and redirecting phone calls.

You will speak with our clients every day, so a friendly, approachable manner is important. You will also need to respond to emergencies promptly and effectively, while helping office operations run smoothly. The role requires you to manage several tasks at once and prioritise them effectively.

Ultimately, a Receptionist’s duties and responsibilities are to ensure the front desk welcomes guests positively, and executes all administrative tasks to the highest quality standards.

Responsibilities

Answering a busy phone line and directing calls appropriately

Greet and welcome guests as soon as they arrive at the office, making the staff member aware of their arrival and directing them to the relevant meeting room/seating area;

Answer, screen and forward incoming phone calls. Taking detailed messages when a member of staff is unavailable.

Management of incoming and outgoing post

Arranging couriers and parcel services

Ensure reception area and meeting rooms are tidy and presentable

Providing refreshments for guests

Provide basic and accurate information in-person and via phone/email

Check voicemails left overnight. Monitor voicemail and the general enquiries inbox frequently throughout the day, forwarding messages and enquiries to the appropriate person or department.

Maintain office security by following safety procedures and controlling access via the reception desk

Archive closed files in the case management system and arrange for physical files to be sent to the remote archive storage facility

Ordering office stationery and business cards

Preparing invoices and taking payments (training will be provided)

Arranging office appointments and booking meeting rooms for fee earners and updating diaries

Ensuring Kitchen and office supplies are stocked, including general office refreshments

Assisting the Criminal Defence Department in opening of new case files onto the case management system (training will be provided)

Requirements

Confident phone manner and ability to handle high call volumes with patience and efficiency

Empathy and professionalism when working with people in distressing or sensitive situations

Strong organisational skills and attention to detail

A team player who is also happy working independently

Proficiency in Microsoft Office

Professional attitude and appearance

Solid written and verbal communication skills

Ability to be resourceful and proactive when issues arise

Multitasking and time-management skills, with the ability to prioritise tasks
